shortDescription: Real stacked z-levels for 1.6: a buildable sky level above and a solid rock basement below, fully simulated as linked pocket maps with live see-through open air and cross-level pawn AI.
body:
# As above, So below

## Pitch
Real, robust z-levels capped at three per column: one sky level above, the surface, one basement below. Every level is a real simulated map. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from the sky level with a live view of the surface below; (2) performance via caching, incremental grids, and event-driven work.

## Locked decisions
- Standalone C# + Harmony only (no Prepatcher, no MultiFloors dependency).
- Cap: 3 levels per column, enforced in LevelMapGen and PlaceWorker_ABStairs.
- Upper-level rules match Z-Levels beta semantics, with documented deviations: floor removal only drops things when the exposed terrain is open air; bomb-punched rooftop holes deferred.
- Basement: 100% solid mineable rock matching surface geology, fogged, thick-roofed; vanilla collapse rules intact.
- Robustness: ABGuard kill switches; HarmonyBoot per-class patching; sync handlers shut down on error, renderer fails open to opaque-below.
- All player-facing text: vanilla sentence case, ASCII only, no long dashes.

## How it works (end of T1.5)
- Core (T0): LevelComp registry on pocket maps aligned 1:1, ground comp as column controller, parent.Tile set for real day/night + geology; stairs pairs that generate levels on completion; use-stairs job with safe transfer; PageUp/PageDown camera-preserving level view.
- Sky mountains (GenStep_ABSkyTerrain): solid mass contracted one cell (walkable ledge ring), mineable rock core under thick rock roof, fog only two erosions deep (two visible face rows). Thin-roof overhang = open air; constructed roofs below = rooftop terrain.
- Fog lifecycle: interior fogged at gen; guaranteed reveal on mineable removal via ThingDespawned handlers (sky + basement); landings unfog their 3x3.
- See-below renderer (Harmony): surface section submeshes at y=-2.5 under the sky map; the surface's LIGHTING OVERLAY is relocated to y=-0.15 and its FOG OF WAR to y=-0.10 (both depth-occluded under solid sky cells), so the view below shows true time-of-day light, lamp glow, and player knowledge; the lighting material's color is per-frame shared state, syncing day/night for free. Subtle dim quad at y=-0.05 (default 12%, scribe key belowDimLight). Live dynamic things below via DrawPos offset flag. Camera far clip 65.5 -> 70. TEMP: one-launch diagnostic warning logs sky glow / celestial / weather numbers, remove after verification.
- Root cause note (2026-07-18): the recurring fogged-looking upper level was neither fog nor a lighting bug: the sky level lights correctly (including night), but the old below-view drew the surface full-bright, so at dusk/night the ground read sunny while the player's level was correctly dark. Real lighting in the below-view resolves the mismatch.
- Live sync (LevelSync via MapEvents): roof below governs rooftop above live; sky floors write constructed roofs below; things over open air fall with Z-Levels-style consequences.

## Quadruple pass log
T1 reentrancy verified; T1.1 far clip 92%; T1.2 contraction 90%; T1.3 fog band 90%; T1.4 mining reveal 90%; T1.5 lighting/fog-in-below-view 85% (diagnostic in place). Polish backlog: lower pawns' far-zoom silhouettes; water-depth submeshes below; natural-roof removal under sky mountains; bomb holes in rooftops.

## Tranche plan
- T0 DONE, T1 through T1.5 CODE DONE (T1.5 awaiting in-game verification).
- T2: movement: stair graph, cross-level pathing, drafted moves, pawns auto-use stairs for jobs, non-surface stair placement.
- T3 (next after T1 sign-off, user-requested): cross-map stockpiles/hauling, storage, bills across levels.
- T4: systems: temperature/weather sync, power across levels, threat policy, map-removal cleanup, profiling; renderer polish.

## Status
T1.5 compiled green, pushed. Pending in-game verification at BOTH day and night: consistent lighting between levels, visible rock faces by day, fog reveal on mining readable in daylight.
